Complete Ground Rules for the 2026 PRCA Playoff Series Finale can be found online at www.prorodeo.org.

FORMAT: ALL EVENTS - The Finale will be two go-rounds, back to back, performance to performance, with a top eight semi-finals followed by a top four finals. Contestants will be placed in the first four performances based on their pay-off series points standings. The following number rankings in the Playoff Series Standings will correspond with only the contestants who actually enter the Finale (for example, if the #1 ranked contestant does not enter and the #2 ranked contestant does enter, the #2 ranked contestant will assume the position as the #1 ranked contestant). If there is a tie for any of the rankings, a random draw by PROCOM will determine where each of the tied contestants will be placed. The #13 position in all events will be occupied by the qualifier from the NFR Open in Colorado Springs. The contestants placed in the first and second performances will be the contestants who correspond with the following rankings: #2, #3, #6, #7, #10, #11, #14, #15, #18, #19, #22, and #23. The contestants placed in the third and fourth performances will be the contestants who correspond with the following rankings: #1, #4, #5, #8, #9, #12, #13, #16, #17, #20, #21, and #24. The lowest ranked contestants (based on these rankings) will compete first, and the highest ranked contestants will compete last for the first go-round. The second go-round will be the reverse order of the first go-round. No trades will be allowed. In the Team Roping event, the 24 headers who qualify must rope with the 24 heelers who qualify. The 48 contestants who constitute the 24 teams will be ranked #1 through #48 based on Playoff Series points. The team will be placed in the position that corresponds with the highest ranked partner of the team using the same placement procedure as used for the other events. The #13 position in the Team Roping event will be occupied by the qualifying team from the NFR Open (or the highest ranked partner of the qualifying team from the NFR Open if the two team partners are roping with different qualified partners at this event). If a contestant's partner is drawn out due to qualification, that header or heeler will be randomly drawn a partner by PROCOM from among the other heelers or headers whose partners were drawn out due to qualification.

ALL EVENTS - Since the entry closing times for Puyallup and Sioux Falls occur after the entry closing time of other rodeos with dates that conflict with Puyallup and Sioux Falls, contestants who are placed in positions at other rodeos that conflict with their position at Puyallup or Sioux Falls will be allowed to draw out of the conflicting rodeo as long as they draw out through PROCOM by the turn out deadline of the conflicting rodeo.

ALL EVENTS - PROCOM will attempt to replace any contestant who notifies a turn-out, doctor's release or visible injury through PROCOM prior to the turn-out deadline for the first go-round of competition. The alternate list for replacements will be based on Playoff Series standings as August 24, 2026.
ENTRY FEES - BB, SB, BR, TD, SW AND TR will be $500 per contestant and will be paid by the PRCA.
COMPLETE CINCH PLAYOFF GROUND RULES can be found by clicking on the red link above.

detailLines: Pendleton OR NPP
September 14-15
Pendleton Extreme Bulls Tour Finale
ARENA: Happy Canyon Arena
ADDRESS: 1601 West Gate
PERFS: 2 Perfs: September 14- 8:00 PM; September 15- 8:00 PM
EVENTS: BR @ $150000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES:
PERMITS: BR
GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANT - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Thurs., Sept. 10 between 9 AM and 11 AM. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
GRACE PERIOD - Will expire one hour after entries close.

QUALIFICATIONS: 26 minimum entries. The top 20 contestants who enter based on 2026 X-bulls Standings as of September 6, 2026 will be accepted as entries. No exemptions. 6 will advance from the Wild Card round.

FORMAT: The first performance on Monday, Sept. 14 will include the Wild Card round followed by the first go-round of the X-bulls Finale. The second performance on Tuesday, Sept. 15 will include the second and third go-rounds of the X-bulls Finale. 22 entries will be accepted for the Wild Card Round which will include the 20 highest ranked contestants based on 2026 X-Bulls standings, who enter and who are not already accepted as entries among the top 20 for the X-Bulls Finale plus the first place winner of the Albuquerque X-Bulls event and the first place winner of the Lewiston X-Bulls event. If the winner of the Albuquerque and Lewiston events are already accepted as entries for the Wild Card round or the X-Bulls Finale due to qualifications, the next highest ranked contestant in the 2026 X-Bulls standings will be accepted for those positions (will not exceed 22). The top 6 based on highest scores in the Wild Card round will advance to the X-Bulls Finale for a total of 26 contestants in the Finale. If ties result in more than 6 to advance, the tied contestant(s) with the highest ranking in the X-Bulls Standings will advance. If there are less than 6 qualified rides in the Wild Card Round, any remaining positions to be filled in the X-Bulls Finale (not to exceed 26) will be based on 2026 X-Bulls Standings.
CHECK-IN - Contestants must check-in or notify arena secretary 1 hour prior to the start of the event. Failure to do so will result in an alternate contestant being selected and allowed to compete.

REPLACEMENTS: Contestants who turn out of the X-Bulls Finale (includes DR's and VIR's through Procom) may be replaced by contestants on the alternate list. There will be two alternate lists. The alternate list for the Wild Card Round will include the contestants who entered but were drawn out due to qualifications. The order of the Wild Card Alternate List will be based on ranking in the 2026 X-Bulls standings. The alternate list for the X-Bulls Finale will include the contestants who competed in the Wild Card Round who did not advance to the X-Bulls Finale. The order of X-Bulls Finale Alternate List will be based on rankings in the X-Bulls standings. Only contestants who turn out of the first go-round of the X-Bulls Finale will be replaced (includes DR's and VIR's through Procom). Contestants who turn out of the X-Bulls Finale will be replaced by a contestant who is already placed in the Wild Card Round. The alternate contestant who is being moved from his position in the Wild Card Round to the position in the X-Bulls Finale will be replaced by the first available alternate from the Wild Card Alternate List. If the contestant that notified the turn-out is not replaced by an alternate, he will be responsible for the $35 fee and the rodeo will count towards the official rodeo count. Any non-notified turn-out will be responsible for the $35 fee and the rodeo will count towards the official rodeo count, If a contestant properly doctor releases, he will not be responsible for entry fees nor will the event be applied to his official rodeo count. If a contestant turns out of this event after the stock draw and a replacement is not found, he will be charged a $500 turn out fine.

PAY-OFF: $12,000 of the total amount in the payoff will be allotted to the pay-off for the Wild Card Round. The Wild Card Round will pay six places. Percentages paid for places will be in accordance with the rulebook. Money won in the Wild Card Round will not count towards X-Bulls or Circuit Standings. Money won in the Wild Card Round will count towards World Standings and money won qualifications. The pay-off for the X-Bulls Finale will be in accordance with the PRCA Rule Book for three go-rounds and an average. The winner of the average of the X-Bulls Finale will be the be the Event winner. The highest ranked contestant based on X-Bulls Standings after the X-Bulls Finale will be the X-Bulls Champion.

NOTE - In order for money won at this event to count for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo or the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings, during the 2026 season, a contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of forty (40) PRCA rodeos during the 2026 rodeo year. Money won will count for PRCA World Standings and Xtreme Bulls Standings. It will not count for All Around standings, circuit standings, nor will the event be applied to a contestant's required circuit participation count. EF'S: No EF plus $35 Central Entry Office/Supplemental Insurance Fee ($35 total).
STK CONT.: Various

Only actual contestant allowed gate access.
ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal. The alternate list for this event will be based on 2026 permit standings.
ALL EVENTS - The "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Fri., Oct. 2 between 9 AM and 12 PM. See Rodeo Entry Page of the business journal.
ALL EVENTS - Entry fees will be $225 and will be paid by the PRCA.

QUALIFICATIONS: The top 10 permit members (which includes any contestant who was a permit member for any part of the 2026 rodeo season) in each event, who enter based on 2026 money won as a permit member, will be accepted. Any contestant who is ranked in the top 30 of 2026 PRCA world standings as of Sept. 8, 2026 in his respective event will not be eligible to be accepted as an entry for the Waco permit finals. In the Team Roping, the top 10 headers, based on 2026 money won as a permit member while competing as a header, and the top 10 heelers, based on 2026 money won as a permit member while competing as a heeler, will be accepted. This includes any contestant who was a permit member for any part of the 2026 rodeo season. The top 10 headers who are accepted must rope with the top 10 heelers who enter. If a contestant enters without a partner or if a contestant's partner is drawn out due to qualifications, a partner will be randomly drawn for him from among the other contestants whose partners were drawn out due to qualifications.
ATTENTION: The first place winner in each event will be accepted as an entry at Rodeo Houston in 2027.
FORMAT: 3 go-rounds.
PAY-OFF: Go-rounds and average will pay 4 places. Money won at this event will not count towards World Standings or Circuit Standings. It will count towards 2027 money won qualifications.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Must sign the PRCA Release and Waiver and Choice of Venue form prior to competition.
BB, SB, BR RE-RIDES - After all replacements have been made, any remaining available animals that were notified as turn outs, will be used prior to using the designated re-rides.

ALL CONTESTANTS WITH ANIMALS - All Texas Animal Health Commission requirements must be followed. Current coggins test within the last 12 months. Out of state competitors should refer to TAHC for current requirements.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Are required to wear a provided back number which must be worn and displayed in its entirety at all times in the competition arena.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes or a re-run is given for any other reason, the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into the herd.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Are required to check-in at the rodeo secretary's office between 3 PM and 5 PM prior to the first performance.

LIVESTOCK - Stock must be inspected by the Livestock Superintendent at the time of arrival and must be accompanied by current certified veterinary health papers and certificates as required by Texas Law. Sore, lame, sick, or injured animals will not be accepted and payment will not be issued for these animals. This includes any animal with a wound that, in the PRCA judge's discretion, is cosmetically questionable. Bred mares in late term of pregnancy or mares with colts will not be accepted. All bulls' horns must be tipped per PRCA rules. All livestock must have an ownership brand and identification brand in compliance with the PRCA Rule Book.
NOTE - 2026 Permit Finals ground rules can be found in PBJ by click on the red link above.

Qualifier TE Only National Western Rodeo

EVENTS: TD SW TR-HD, TR-HL
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: TD-$200; SW-$200; TR-$200
PERMITS: TD SW TR
GROUND RULES: ATTENTION ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestants must have their 2027 membership renewed to be accepted as entries for the Dever Qualifier.
ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal.
ALL CONTESTANTS - All participants agree to be bound by the terms and conditions of the PRCA Bylaws and Official Rodeo Rules and these Ground Rules.
ALL CONTESTANTS - All contestants must check-in with the rodeo secretary in the "Show Office" and sign a release of liability before competing in this rodeo.

ALL CONTESTANTS WITH HORSES - Must have proof of current Coggins test and current health papers. Health papers must be checked at the Stalling Office prior to unloading horses. All stalls will be available to contestants at $20 per night (includes one bag of shavings), beginning Monday, October 19 after 4:00 p.m., on a first come first served basis. Parking of contestant's vehicles and horse trailers must be in area designated by the National Western Stock Show parking lot operator.
TD, SW, and TR Qualifications for Denver, CO - January 14-24, 2027 and the Denver Qualifier - October 20-22, 2026:
80 minimum entries for the Denver Rodeo. No compensation. No slack. No exemptions.

The top 30 in the final 2026 PRCA World Standings, the top 5 who enter based on 2027 money won, the top 5 from the 2026 Mountain States Circuit Standings who enter and who are not already qualified in the previous two categories, and 40 from the Denver Qualifier (October 20-22) will be accepted as entries for a total of 80 entries for the Denver Rodeo. The contestants who were among the top 30 in the final 2026 World Standings in each event will be accepted as entries for the Denver rodeo if they enter and will not be accepted as entries for the Qualifier. All others may enter the Denver Qualifier on October 20-22. If not all of the top 30 from the 2026 PRCA World Standings in an event enter the Denver Rodeo, the remaining unfilled positions will be filled by contestants based on 2027 money won (not to exceed a total of 80 entries). For example, if only 28 from the Final 2026 World Standings enter the Denver Rodeo, 7 will be accepted based on 2027 money won, 5 from the 2026 Mountain States Circuit Standings, and 40 from the Denver Qualifier, for a total of 80. In the Team Roping, headers and heelers will qualify separately using the same qualifications The 80 headers who qualify must rope with the 80 heelers who qaulify. There will be a grace period for Team Ropers to designate partners.
QUALIFICATIONS for the Denver Qualifier: TD - 145 minimum entries; SW - 155 minimum entries; TR - 120 minimum entries.

FORMAT: 40 qualifying contestants or teams from the qualifier will be placed in the performances at the National Western Stock Show, along with the 40 contestants (or teams) already entered. The 40 qualifying contestants or teams will be top ten from the first go-round (plus splits), the top ten from the second go-round that have not already qualified from the first go-round (plus splits), and the remaining positions (not to exceed 40) will be filled from the fastest times in the average after the first and second go-rounds. If there are ties, the tied contestant (or team) with the single fastest time will advance to the performances at the National Western Rodeo. If still tied, the tied contestant with the highest ranking in the 2026 PRCA World Standings for that event will advance. All 80 contestants (or teams) that qualify for the Denver National Western Rodeo will have a grace period to change preferences and/or buddy groups on Wed., Dec. 16 between 9 AM and 4 PM.
TD - Two go-rounds. Both run Tues., Oct. 20 at 9 AM.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerk down as long as criteria are in compliance with the jerk down policy.
SW - Two go-rounds. Both run Wed., Oct. 21 at 9 AM.
TR - Only two loops allowed.
TR - Two go-rounds. Both run Thurs., Oct. 22 at 9 AM.

SW - The steer must fall clean when a throw is attempted. If a clean fall is not achieved and the motion stops, the steer must be allowed to regain his feet before being thrown. If the steer is not allowed to regain his feet when instructed by the judge, the contestant will be disqualified.
TD, SW - $30 stock charge for cards and permits.
TR - $15 stock charge per man for cards and permits.
TE - The qualifier and the National Western Rodeo performances will each count as separate rodeos. All entries are official, unless contestant specifies otherwise at time of entry.
TD, SW, TR - Payoff will be in accordance with the rule book.
STK CONT.: Various

detailLines: San Angelo TX

Cinch Roping Fiesta
ARENA: Fiesta Arena

PERFS: 2 Perfs: October 24- 1:00 PM; October 25- 12:00 PM
EVENTS: TD @ $25000 SR @ $12500
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: TD-$1075; SR-$750
PERMITS: TD SR

GROUND RULES: ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" and "walk-up replacement" policies will be in effect. The alternate list will be based on 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing).

QUALIFICATIONS:TD - 40 entries. The top 34 from 2026 PRCA World Standings that enter will be accepted. 5 will advance from the qualifying event and 1 committee invite (must be a PRCA member). Entry fees will be $1,075 plus a $35 stock charge.
ALL CONTESTANTS - TD will occur on Saturday, October 24th. SR will occur on Sunday, October 25th.
TD - Electric eye will be used. The length of the score will be approved by the event representative.

TD STOCK DRAW - The long go-rounds and short round will be drawn prior to the beginning of the first go-round. There will be on animal for every entry plus adequate extras. The extras will be designated by the event representative or his designee. After the completion of each go-round, all extras will be run and will be used to replace any sick or injured animals. The misdraw procedure will not be used. Fresh animals will be used in the finals.

TD PAYOFF: The following amounts could decrease due to doctors released contestants who are not replaced (which would result in less entry fee money in the total payoff) or the amount could increase due to turned out contestants who are replaced (which would result in more entry fee money in the total payoff).

TD FORMAT AND PAYOFF: Two go-rounds plus a top 12 finals. $25,000 (added purse) plus $43,000 (entry fees: 40 contestants x $1,075) equals $68,000. $68,000 minus 6% ($4,080) equals $63,920 to be included in the payoff. Each of the first two go-rounds will pay 5 places: $4,610.10 (30%) for 1st, $3,841.75 (25%) for 2nd, $3,073.40 (20%) for 3rd, $2,305.05 (15%) for 4th, and $1,536.70 (10%) for 5th for a total of $15,367 paid out for each go-round. The finals will pay 4 places: $4,000 for 1st, $3,000 for 2nd, $2,000 for 3rd, and $1,000 for 4th for a total of $10,000 paid out for the finals. The average will pay 5 places: $6,955.80 (30%) for 1st, $5,796.50 (25%) for 2nd, $4,637.20 (20%) for 3rd, $3,477.90 (15%) for 4th and $2,318.60 (10%) for 5th for a total of $23,186 paid out for the average.

SR QUALIFICATIONS - 30 minimum entries. The top 24 from 2026 PRCA World Standings that enter will be accepted. 6 will advance from the qualifying event. Three go-rounds. The competition order of the third go-round will be based on times in the average after the first two go-rounds. The contestants with no qualified times in the average after the first two go-rounds will compete first in the third go-round, followed by the contestants with the slowest times in the average. The contestants with the fastest times in the average will compete last. Entry fees are $750. $80 stock charge per go-round.
SR - The qualifying event will be held in Graham, TX on October 16, 2026.
SR - Electric eye barrier may be used. The length of the score will be approved by the event representative. All rounds will be drawn prior to the first go-round.
SR PAYOFF: Pay-off will be in accordance with the rulebook for three go-rounds and an average.

TD - If a contestant who is not an active PRCA card or permit member qualifies to advance from the qualifying round to the San Angelo Cinch Roping Fiesta performance in the TD, his membership application and dues must be received by the PRCA office no later than 3 PM on Fri., Oct. 23. If his membership application is not received by the deadline, the next highest ranked contestant from the qualifying event will be accepted. (Member records 719.528.4747, Member records fax 719.548.4868).

NOTE: In order for money won at this event to count for qualify for the 2027 National Finals Rodeo or the 2027 Rookie of the Year Standings, a TD contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA Rodeos during the 2027 rodeo year and a SR contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 15 PRCA rodeos, during the 2027 rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count for all Around Standings, circuit standings nor will the event be applied towards a contestant's required circuit participation count. For information regarding the qualifying rounds, go to www.sanangelorodeo.com or call 325.653.7785.
STK CONT.: Various

detailLines: Davie FL NPP
November 13-15
Southeastern Circuit Finals
ARENA: Bergeron Rodeo Grounds
ADDRESS: 4931 Davie Rd.
PERFS: 3 Perfs: November 13- 7:30 PM; November 14- 7:30 PM; November 15- 2:00 PM
EVENTS: BB SB BR TD SW @ $10000 + $18088 SPON TR-HD, TR-HL @ $10000 + $36176 SPON
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$225; SB-$225; BR-$225; TD-$225; SW-$225; TR-$225
PERMITS: CIR - BB SB BR TD SW TR

GROUND RULES: Only actual contestant allowed gate access. All CDC, Florida Department of Health, and Broward County Guidelines will be followed. The cutoff date for the 2026 Southeastern Circuit Finals will be Sept. 30, 2026.
Total money above includes estimated committee purse of $10,000, estimated PRCA matching funds of $4,000, estimated sponsor money of $14,088 and estimated $3 is TBD.

ALL CONTESTANTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Fri., Oct. 23 between 9 AM and 12 PM. Re-entries will be accepted if the number of entries for an event at the original entry closing time is less than limit defined in the ground rules. If more contestants enter during the "re-entry" period than there are positions available, the contestants accepted will be based on the qualification procedures defined in the Circuit Finals ground rules. Under no circumstances will a contestant who entered during the re-entry period be able to displace a contestant who entered during the original entry period. If a contestant TO's or DR's prior to the "re-entry" period, that position may be filled during the "re-entry" period.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Must check-in with secretary by 2 PM on Nov. 13th to receive the packets. Late check-in fine will be $100.
MUG SHOTS - Contestants must have photo taken by Fri., Nov. 13th by 2 PM. After deadline $25 fine. Cowboy attire required.

ALL CONTESTANTS - PARKING: There will be a separate parking area for Southeastern Circuit Contestants, Stock Contractors, and Personnel. Each Contestant, Stock Contractor, and Contract Personnel will receive one parking pass. Additional Parking Passes will not be available. Trailer Parking is limited. You will be provided a 24'x50' parking space. Contestants must check in with Parking Attendant prior to parking and setting your trailer. If you come in after hours, you must check with Parking Attendant the following morning. If you park in a space not specified by the Parking Attendant, you will be asked to move. For all illegally parked trailers the Southeast Circuit will receive a fine, and you will be responsible to the Southeastern Circuit for the fine.

ALL CONTESTANTS - PASSES: A. Each Stock Contracting Company and Contract Personnel will be given one Companion Pass. Each Contestant will receive one Companion Pass. PRCA Membership cards or PRCA membership companion passes will not be accepted for admittance. B. Stock Contractors, Contract Personnel, and Contestants needing additional tickets will need to be purchased from the arena box office or online ticket sales.
STOCK CONTRACTORS: No consideration will be given for death, or loss. Feed and housing of Livestock will be furnished from check-in time to the conclusion of the Southeastern Circuit Finals Rodeo.

STOCK DELIVERY/LOADING/USE: A. Stock must be delivered to the Bergeron Rodeo Grounds by Thurs., November 12, 2026. B. Animals that are unfit, sick, or lame prior to delivery ("delivery" defined as having completely exited the trailer upon arrival during designated stock delivery timeframe) will not be accepted or paid for.

C. All riding event livestock must be delivered with a readable permanent ownership and number brand in accordance with the PRCA Rulebook. D. All bulls must be tipped in accordance with PRCA Rule R7.10.5 prior to delivery to Bergeron Rodeo Grounds.
ALL CONTESTANTS - See parking attendant prior to parking trailers.
ALL EVENTS - Will pay four places in all go rounds and average.
QUALIFICATIONS: Top 12.
COMPLETE CIRCUIT FINALS GROUND RULES can be found by clicking on the red link above.
STK CONT.: Various
